extracted.intended_audience: general newspaper readers and policymakers interested in wartime communications and defense
extracted.subtask_description: A wartime newspaper article reporting military actions, government orders, and related policy developments (Associated Press-style coverage). Emphasizes facts, official statements, eyewitness accounts, and excerpts of formal orders affecting national defense communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creation and membership of the Defense Communications Board
rubrics_metrics.description: There is hereby created the 'Defense Communications Board,' hereinafter called the board, consisting of the chairman, Federal Communications Commission; the Chief Signal Officer of the Army; the Director of Naval Communications; the Assistant Secretary of State in charge of the Division of International Communications; and the Assistant Secretary of the Treasury in charge of the Coast Guard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The chairman of the Federal Communications Commission shall be the chairman of the board. In the absence of the designated chairman, temporary chairmanship devolves upon remaining members in specified order (Chief Signal Officer of the Army or Director of Naval Communications). In the absence of any regularly designated member, the represented agency may send an alternate designated by its head, but such alternate shall not serve as chairman. The Assistant Secretary of the Treasury in charge of the Coast Guard is designated as the secretary of the board.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary functions of the Defense Communications Board
rubrics_metrics.description: With the requirements of national defense as a primary consideration, to determine, coordinate and prepare plans for the national defense which will enunciate for and during any national emergency: A. The needs of the armed forces of the United States, of other governmental agencies, of industry and of other civilian activities for radio, wire and cable communication facilities of all kinds; B. The allocation of such portions of governmental and non-governmental radio, wire and cable facilities as may be required to meet the needs of the armed forces, due consideration being given to the needs of other governmental agencies, of industry and of other civilian activities; C. The measures of control, the agencies to exercise this control and the principles under which such control will be exercised over non-military communications to meet defense requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The board shall study the physical aspects of domestic standard broadcasting and shall recommend precautions, supplementary facilities and reallocations as desirable under foreseeable military conditions; it shall also make plans for the speedy and efficacious use of all necessary facilities in time of military emergency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Committee structure, consultation, and reporting requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The board shall appoint such committees as may be necessary to carry out its functions and to provide for continuing studies and for contact with other government agencies and with the civil communication industry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Except as otherwise instructed, committees have no power to make final disposition of matters presented; they shall express findings and recommendations by written report. Minority reports may be submitted. The board and committees shall call for consultation such representatives of other government agencies and of the civilian communication industry as may be deemed advisable. Reports containing the findings and recommendations of the board shall be submitted to the President for final action through one of his administrative assistants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role of the Interdepartment Radio Advisory Committee during emergency
rubrics_metrics.description: During any war in which the United States is a belligerent, or any national emergency, the existing Interdepartment Radio Advisory Committee shall act as a committee of the board, but only in an advisory capacity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While acting as an advisory committee, all of its reports, recommendations or communications normally prepared for submission to the President shall instead be submitted to the board for consideration from the standpoint of national defense and for disposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit on censorship authority
rubrics_metrics.description: The board shall take no cognizance of matters pertaining to censorship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although the board will not deal with censorship, it will study physical aspects of broadcasting and recommend precautions, supplementary facilities and reallocations as desirable under foreseeable military conditions and plan for use of facilities in military emergencies.
